back: Documents are mixtures of topics and topics are distributions over words; both have Dirichlet priors.
A distribution over probability vectors; $\alpha<1$ favours sparse vectors, $\alpha>1$ near-uniform ones. Conjugate to the categorical.
Resample one variable at a time from its conditional given all others; leaves the joint invariant and is always accepted; needs ergodicity (no zero conditionals).
$P(z_{di}=k)\propto(n_{dk}+\alpha)\frac{n_{kw}+\beta}{n_k+V\beta}$ with the current token removed from the counts.
$\theta$ and $\phi$ are integrated out thanks to Dirichlet-multinomial conjugacy; only the assignments $z$ are sampled.

front: Estimating theta and phi after sampling

back: ndk $(D,K)$, nkw $(K,V)$, nk $(K,)$, theta $(D,K)$, phi $(K,V)$; rows of theta, phi sum to 1.
Raw word counts (bag of words), after removing stop words and very rare/frequent terms; not TF-IDF.
Score of how often a topic's top words co-occur in real text (NPMI-based, e.g. c_v). Higher is better.
Fraction of distinct words among the top words of all topics; low values mean redundant topics.
Sentence embeddings -> UMAP reduction -> HDBSCAN clustering (with outlier label) -> class-based TF-IDF to name topics.
LDA: mixtures, long documents, cheap. BERTopic: short text, semantic topics, hard assignment, embedding cost and truncation.

front: Is the choice of K learned?
back: No, K is a hyperparameter: compare several values by coherence and by reading the topics; check stability over seeds.
